references.text: Describes the creation of vegetation on the third day, which relates to the conditions before vegetation grew in Genesis 2:5.
Explains how a mist/spring rose from the earth and watered the entire surface of the ground – the solution to the situation described in 2:5 where it had not yet rained.
After the fall, humanity is to work the land (la'avod et-ha'adamah), which corresponds with 2:5 where there was no human yet to cultivate the ground.
God sends rain on land where no human lives – relevant to the theme of God's sovereignty over rain, as in Genesis 2:5 where the Lord God had not yet caused it to rain.
God commands the clouds not to send rain, illustrating God's control over precipitation – relevant for Genesis 2:5 where it is said that the Lord God had not caused it to rain on the earth.
